checked: Checked the summary and prose for the listed stock phrases; none occur. Sentence openings vary across definitions, instructions, and explanations.

Core Concept introduces change = later value minus earlier value before #7 uses 65 minus 50 and #9 uses 27 minus 18.
Core Concept introduces share = sector angle divided by 360 degrees and part amount = share times total before #8 uses 180/360 and one-half times 120. Ranking in #5 needs no additional formula.

Each of the nine placeholders is one line specifying the actual visual needed by its own question. Charts include titles, labels, ticks, values, and units where relevant.

Comic and cartoon specifications identify actions, expressions, labels, and contrasts. The table specification gives every heading and cell. These are load-bearing visual-media questions, so prose need not replace the figures.
Panel, symbolism, labels, exaggeration, caricature, analogy, juxtaposition, irony, legend, unit, axis, scale, truncated axis, sector, row, and column receive local explanations.

findings.quote: With equal radii, larger sectors have larger angles and areas, so they show larger shares.
findings.problem: Radii is needed to understand the stated condition for comparing sectors, but the lesson never explains that a radius runs from the center of a circle to its edge. No supplied prerequisite teaches the term.

checked: The lesson explains how panel sequence supports a conclusion and how cartoon labels, features, contrast, and irony support a message.

Chart teaching connects bar length with amounts and baseline, line positions with ordered changes, pie angles and areas with shares, and row-column intersections with table entries. Worked examples apply these mechanisms.
The lesson limits cartoon conclusions to visible evidence and does not give symbols a fixed meaning.

Bar ranking is qualified by scale direction; zero baselines apply to total bar lengths; nonzero line axes are allowed with label checks. Pie comparisons specify equal radii, and color means amount only if the legend says so. Table reading requires the correct category, period, value, and unit.
